# The GoRex-borrowed GUI, by its own controls (tests/run.sh puts a folder
# at @DIR@). Nothing here is checked by pixels: the labels, palette rows and
# screens are read back as text.
#
# Tab labels: the program, and where (a short folder).
type:cd @DIR@/deep/a/b/c/proj && vim
key:enter
wait:2.5
expect-tab:Vim · …/c/proj
# A split: two panes, then a fresh shell in place of the new one.
key:cmd+d
wait:1.0
type:echo OLD-SHELL
key:enter
wait:0.5
key:cmd+shift+p
wait:0.4
type:restart shell
wait:0.3
expect-palette:Restart Shell in Pane
key:enter
wait:1.5
expect-not:OLD-SHELL
type:echo NEW-SHELL
key:enter
wait:0.8
expect:NEW-SHELL
# Zoom says so in the tab's row.
key:cmd+shift+enter
wait:0.4
expect-tab:2 panes, zoomed
key:cmd+shift+enter
wait:0.4
# ⌘P lists every pane; typing a program finds its pane, Return goes there.
key:cmd+p
wait:0.5
type:vim
wait:0.3
expect-palette:Vim · …/c/proj
key:enter
wait:0.6
# The palette says when nothing matches rather than shrinking away.
key:cmd+shift+p
wait:0.4
type:zzqqxx
wait:0.3
expect-palette:No matches
key:escape
wait:0.3
# Rename the tab in place; Return keeps it, the keyboard goes back.
key:cmd+shift+r
wait:0.4
type:build box
key:enter
wait:0.5
expect-tab:build box
# A name being typed survives the other tabs' updates: tab 2's program
# changes while tab 1 is renamed.
tab:new
type:sleep 1.2; vim
key:enter
tab:1
key:cmd+shift+r
wait:0.4
type:kept name
wait:2.5
key:enter
wait:0.5
expect-tab:kept name
expect-tab:Vim
# A tab opening meanwhile keeps what was typed.
key:cmd+shift+r
wait:0.4
type:second name
tab:new
wait:0.3
expect-tab:second name
# ⌘P finds a pane by the name its tab was given.
key:cmd+p
wait:0.5
type:second name
wait:0.3
expect-palette:Tab 1
key:escape
wait:0.3
# ⌘T opens in the folder of the pane you were in, not at home. (Reached
# by a relative cd: only the new tab's pwd can print the whole path.)
type:cd @DIR@
key:enter
wait:0.5
type:cd elsewhere/here
key:enter
wait:0.6
tab:here
wait:0.8
type:pwd
key:enter
wait:0.6
expect:@DIR@/elsewhere/here
